alternatives.transcript: An agency prospect is a single real world business that we might be able to win as a client. We have 200 of them in the database right now. If you click the object name at the top of this post, it opens straight into the CRM. So you can go and look while I talk. Think of a prospect as the very first card we deal. Not a person, not a conversation, not a deal. Just a business. The shop itself, sitting in a city, doing a kind of Auto body shops. Detailing shops. Window tinting. Those are our niches. Every other object in this whole library hangs off a prospect, so this is the one to understand first. Inside a prospect row, you will find the shop's name and a slug, which is a clean web friendly version of that name. You will find the niche, so we know what kind of work they do, and the city and region, so we know where they are. Then the practical contact stuff. A phone number we can ring, and an email address with a confidence score attached, which tells us how sure we are that the address is genuinely theirs and not a guess. There is also an AI fit score out of 100, and a fit reason field which is the actual sentence explaining why we rated them that way. So you can always challenge the number, and a tech stack field which is the list of tools we detected the shop is already running. Why does this object matter so much? Because nothing else in the funnel exists without one underneath it. Leads attach to prospects. Calls get placed to the phone numbers stored here. Scripts and campaigns are aimed at the niches recorded here. This is the spite of the whole database. Get it wrong and the damage spreads in every direction. If somebody merges two shops badly or deletes a prospect because it looks like a duplicate, you do not just lose one row you orphan leads that had no other home, you leave calls pointing at nothing, and the reporting quietly starts lying to you. That is exactly why this is the object we protect most carefully. Where is it actually used in the day to day? We find these shops out in the wild, mostly from their own public websites and from the directory listings that the agency listings object tracks. Once a shop is in here, the fit score decides who gets worked first, so a high scoring tinting shop and a good market jumps the queue over a low scoring one. Then the phone number stored on the prospect row is literally the number the dialer calls. And as deals progress, the Weibel field is how we mark where they sit. New, working, won, lost. When you join the organization and you know nothing else, open this object first. It is the map of who we are trying to reach.
